audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Irelia levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items and called 4-5 and 6 even, while every reason underneath says the opposite: whys[1] 'opens trades before my Flawless Duet exists', whys[2] 'out-trades my fresh E', whys[3] 'I lose the extended skirmish', whys[4] 'neutralizing my entire DPS pattern', whys[5] 'the trade math flips against me', whys[6] 'Camille is the stronger scaler'. Both early and mid open with 'Camille owns these levels' and 'This stays her lane'. The 48.56% win rate agrees with the prose, not the labels.
audit.why: Hookshot's wall-stun opens trades before Flawless Duet exists, Precision Protocol's second cast carries true damage, Tactical Sweep heals her out of extended trades, and The Hextech Ultimatum removes the minions Bladesurge resets off. Camille owns everything from level 2 onward.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 through 6 set to Camille in both layers, ratings re-scored, and diff moved from EVEN 6/10 to TRICKY 7.5/10 with the matching tone.
sources: brief currentText whys[1..6], early, mid, late

audit.whatIsWrong: No Camille cooldown appeared anywhere, and her ultimate was written as 'Hextech Ultimatum' — the packet flagged it and it is right: Riot's name is The Hextech Ultimatum.
audit.why: The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s and 475 range; Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s; Tactical Sweep is 15/14/13/12/11s. A 140-second rank-1 ultimate is the single largest window in the lane.
audit.corrected: Real name and the 140s rank-1 number written into whys[4], spikes[1].text and wants.foe[1]; Tactical Sweep's 15s stated in whys[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interaction errors. (a) The page told the player four times to hold Defiant Dance to block Precision Protocol's second cast — that cast is TRUE damage and Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage, so the reduction does nothing to it. (b) Tactical Sweep's outer half was called true damage in whys[3] and wants.you[1]; Riot's text says extra damage and a heal, not true damage. (c) Adaptive Defenses was never explained — it shields only against the damage type that hit her, which is why Irelia's on-hit magic matters more than her autos here.
audit.why: Riot's text: Irelia W 'takes reduced physical damage during the charge'; Camille Q carries the trueDamage flag; Camille W 'enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille'; Camille P shields 'against their damage type (Physical or Magic)'.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1], dosFull[2], dontsFull[0], dontsFull[1], whys[3] and wants.you[1] rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0] 'Get E-stunned first' and dontsFull[1] 'Fight near walls' both carried generic filler bodies.
audit.why: Precision Protocol is an auto-attack reset, so her burst opens on a wind-up rather than a visible cast; Hookshot requires terrain, so open lane strips her of both engage and escape.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to the real mechanic.
sources: enemyKit E text (pulls herself to a wall)

notes: One deliberate departure from the packet: packet.levelChart gives row 6 (2+ items) to Irelia, but whys[6], spikes[3].text and the late paragraph all say Camille is the stronger scaler and reclaims the duel at two items, and the 48.56% win rate agrees. I set row 6 to Camille. If the packet chart is authoritative over the prose, this row and the three strings behind it need to flip together instead. Following the mirror audit's note, I treated the 'channel/interruptible' and 'untargetable' flags on The Hextech Ultimatum as tooltip-parse misfires — Riot's text describes a dash plus an anchoring zone — so I asserted neither that Flawless Duet cancels it nor that she goes untargetable through it, despite missingInteractions suggesting both.
